NKJV.1: Awake, awake! Put on your strength, O Zion; Put on your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city! For the uncircumcised and the unclean Shall no longer come to you.
NKJV.2: Shake yourself from the dust, arise; Sit down, O Jerusalem!  Loose yourself from the bonds of your neck, O captive daughter of Zion!
NKJV.3: For thus says the LORD:  “You have sold yourselves for nothing, And you shall be redeemed without money.”
NKJV.4: For thus says the Lord GOD: “My people went down at first Into Egypt to dwell there; Then the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.
NKJV.5: Now therefore, what have I here,” says the LORD, “That My people are taken away for nothing? Those who rule over them Make them wail,” says the LORD, “And My name is blasphemed continually every day.
NKJV.6: Therefore My people shall know My name; Therefore they shall know in that day That I am He who speaks: ‘Behold, it is I.’ ”
NKJV.7: How beautiful upon the mountains Are the feet of him who brings good news, Who proclaims peace, Who brings glad tidings of good things, Who proclaims salvation, Who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
NKJV.8: Your watchmen shall lift up their voices, With their voices they shall sing together; For they shall see eye to eye When the LORD brings back Zion.
NKJV.9: Break forth into joy, sing together, You waste places of Jerusalem! For the LORD has comforted His people, He has redeemed Jerusalem.
NKJV.10: The LORD has made bare His holy arm In the eyes of all the nations; And all the ends of the earth shall see The salvation of our God.
NKJV.11: Depart! Depart! Go out from there, Touch no unclean thing; Go out from the midst of her, Be clean, You who bear the vessels of the LORD.
NKJV.12: For you shall not go out with haste, Nor go by flight; For the LORD will go before you, And the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
NKJV.13: Behold, My Servant shall deal prudently;  He shall be exalted and extolled and be very high.
NKJV.14: Just as many were astonished at you, So His visage was marred more than any man, And His form more than the sons of men;
NKJV.15: So shall He sprinkle many nations. Kings shall shut their mouths at Him; For what had not been told them they shall see, And what they had not heard they shall consider.

ESV.1: Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion; put on your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city; for there shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.
ESV.2: Shake yourself from the dust and arise; be seated, O Jerusalem; loose the bonds from your neck, O captive daughter of Zion.
ESV.3: For thus says the LORD: “You were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without money.”
ESV.4: For thus says the Lord GOD: “My people went down at the first into Egypt to sojourn there, and the Assyrian oppressed them for nothing.
ESV.5: Now therefore what have I here,” declares the LORD, “seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Their rulers wail,” declares the LORD, “and continually all the day my name is despised.
ESV.6: Therefore my people shall know my name. Therefore in that day they shall know that it is I who speak; here I am.”
ESV.7: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of happiness, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
ESV.8: The voice of your watchmen — they lift up their voice; together they sing for joy; for eye to eye they see the return of the LORD to Zion.
ESV.9: Break forth together into singing, you waste places of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
ESV.10: The LORD has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.
ESV.11: Depart, depart, go out from there; touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of her; purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of the LORD.
ESV.12: For you shall not go out in haste, and you shall not go in flight, for the LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
ESV.13: Behold, my servant shall act wisely;  he shall be high and lifted up, and shall be exalted.
ESV.14: As many were astonished at you — his appearance was so marred, beyond human semblance, and his form beyond that of the children of mankind —
ESV.15: so shall he sprinkle  many nations. Kings shall shut their mouths because of him, for that which has not been told them they see, and that which they have not heard they understand.

NASB.1: Awake, awake, Clothe yourself in your strength, O Zion; Clothe yourself in your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city; For the uncircumcised and the unclean Will no longer come into you.
NASB.2: Shake yourself from the dust, rise up, O captive Jerusalem; Loose yourself from the chains around your neck, O captive daughter of Zion.
NASB.3: For thus says the LORD, 'You were sold for nothing and you will be redeemed without money.'
NASB.4: For thus says the Lord GOD, 'My people went down at the first into Egypt to reside there; then the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.
NASB.5: 'Now therefore, what do I have here,' declares the LORD, 'seeing that My people have been taken away without cause?' [Again] the LORD declares, 'Those who rule over them howl, and My name is continually blasphemed all day long.
NASB.6: 'Therefore My people shall know My name; therefore in that day I am the one who is speaking, 'Here I am.''
NASB.7: How lovely on the mountains Are the feet of him who brings good news, Who announces peace And brings good news of happiness, Who announces salvation, [And] says to Zion, 'Your God reigns!'
NASB.8: Listen! Your watchmen lift up [their] voices, They shout joyfully together; For they will see with their own eyes When the LORD restores Zion.
NASB.9: Break forth, shout joyfully together, You waste places of Jerusalem; For the LORD has comforted His people, He has redeemed Jerusalem.
NASB.10: The LORD has bared His holy arm In the sight of all the nations, That all the ends of the earth may see The salvation of our God.
NASB.11: Depart, depart, go out from there, Touch nothing unclean; Go out of the midst of her, purify yourselves, You who carry the vessels of the LORD.
NASB.12: But you will not go out in haste, Nor will you go as fugitives; For the LORD will go before you, And the God of Israel [will be] your rear guard.
NASB.13: Behold, My servant will prosper, He will be high and lifted up and greatly exalted.
NASB.14: Just as many were astonished at you, [My people], So His appearance was marred more than any man And His form more than the sons of men.
NASB.15: Thus He will sprinkle many nations, Kings will shut their mouths on account of Him; For what had not been told them they will see, And what they had not heard they will understand.

WEB.1: Awake, awake! Put on your strength, Zion. Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for from now on the uncircumcised and the unclean will no more come into you.
WEB.2: Shake yourself from the dust! Arise, sit up, Jerusalem! Release yourself from the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
WEB.3: For Yahweh says, “You were sold for nothing; and you will be redeemed without money.”
WEB.4: For thus says the Lord Yahweh: “My people went down at the first into Egypt to live there: and the Assyrian has oppressed them without cause.
WEB.5: “Now therefore, what do I do here,” says Yahweh, “seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Those who rule over them mock,” says Yahweh, “and my name is blasphemed continually all day long.
WEB.6: Therefore my people shall know my name. Therefore they shall know in that day that I am he who speaks. Behold, it is I.”
WEB.7: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
WEB.8: Your watchmen lift up their voice, together they sing; for they shall see eye to eye, when Yahweh returns to Zion.
WEB.9: Break out into joy, sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem; for Yahweh has comforted his people. He has redeemed Jerusalem.
WEB.10: Yahweh has made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
WEB.11: Depart, depart, go out from there; touch no unclean thing! Go out from among her! Cleanse yourselves, you who carry Yahweh’s vessels.
WEB.12: For you shall not go out in haste, neither shall you go by flight: for Yahweh will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
WEB.13: Behold, my servant will deal wisely. He will be exalted and lifted up, and will be very high.
WEB.14: Just as many were astonished at you (his appearance was marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men),
WEB.15: so he will cleanse  many nations. Kings will shut their mouths at him: for they will see that which had not been told them; and they will understand that which they had not heard.

NLT.1:
Wake up, wake up, O Zion!
Clothe yourself with strength.
Put on your beautiful clothes, O holy city of Jerusalem,
for unclean and godless people will enter your gates no longer.
NLT.2:
Rise from the dust, O Jerusalem.
Sit in a place of honor.
Remove the chains of slavery from your neck,
O captive daughter of Zion.
NLT.3:
For this is what the LORD says:
“When I sold you into exile,
I received no payment.
Now I can redeem you
without having to pay for you.”
NLT.4: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: “Long ago my people chose to live in Egypt. Now they are oppressed by Assyria.
NLT.5: What is this?” asks the LORD. “Why are my people enslaved again? Those who rule them shout in exultation. My name is blasphemed all day long.
NLT.6: But I will reveal my name to my people, and they will come to know its power. Then at last they will recognize that I am the one who speaks to them.”
NLT.7:
How beautiful on the mountains
are the feet of the messenger who brings good news,
the good news of peace and salvation,
the news that the God of Israel reigns!
NLT.8:
The watchmen shout and sing with joy,
for before their very eyes
they see the LORD returning to Jerusalem.
NLT.9:
Let the ruins of Jerusalem break into joyful song,
for the LORD has comforted his people.
He has redeemed Jerusalem.
NLT.10:
The LORD has demonstrated his holy power
before the eyes of all the nations.
All the ends of the earth will see
the victory of our God.
NLT.11:
Get out! Get out and leave your captivity,
where everything you touch is unclean.
Get out of there and purify yourselves,
you who carry home the sacred objects of the LORD.
NLT.12:
You will not leave in a hurry,
running for your lives.
For the LORD will go ahead of you;
yes, the God of Israel will protect you from behind.
NLT.13:
See, my servant will prosper;
he will be highly exalted.
NLT.14:
But many were amazed when they saw him.
His face was so disfigured he seemed hardly human,
and from his appearance, one would scarcely know he was a man.
NLT.15:
And he will startle many nations.
Kings will stand speechless in his presence.
For they will see what they had not been told;
they will understand what they had not heard about.

AMP.1:
Awake, awake,
Put on your strength, O Zion;
Put on your beautiful garments,
O Jerusalem, the holy city;
For the uncircumcised and the unclean
Will no longer come into you.
AMP.2:
Shake yourself from the dust, arise,
O captive Jerusalem;
Rid yourself of the chains around your neck,
O captive Daughter of Zion.
AMP.3: For the LORD says this, "You were sold for nothing and you will be redeemed, but not with money."
AMP.4: For the Lord GOD says this, "My people went down at the first into Egypt to live there; and [many years later Sennacherib] the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.
AMP.5: But now, what do I have here," declares the LORD, "seeing that My people have been taken away without reason? Those who rule over them howl [with taunting and mockery of salvation]," declares the LORD, "and My name is continually blasphemed all day long.
AMP.6: Therefore My people shall know My Name and what it means. Therefore in that day I am the One who is speaking, 'Here I am.'"
AMP.7:
How beautiful and delightful on the mountains
Are the feet of him who brings good news,
Who announces peace,
Who brings good news of good [things],
Who announces salvation,
Who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
AMP.8:
Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices,
Together they shout for joy;
For they will see face to face
The return of the LORD to Zion.
AMP.9:
Break forth, shout joyfully together,
You ruins of Jerusalem;
For the LORD has comforted His people,
He has redeemed Jerusalem.
AMP.10:
The LORD has bared His holy arm (His infinite power)
Before the eyes of all the nations [revealing Himself as the One by Whom Israel is redeemed from captivity],
That all the ends of the earth may see
The salvation of our God.
AMP.11:
Depart, depart, go out from there (the lands of exile),
Touch no unclean thing;
Go out of the midst of her (Babylon), purify yourselves,
You who carry the articles of the LORD [on your journey from there].
AMP.12:
For you will not go out in a hurry [as when you left Egypt],
Nor will you go in flight [fleeing, as you did from the Egyptians];
For the LORD will go before you,
And the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
AMP.13:
Indeed, My Servant (the Messiah) will act wisely and prosper;
He will be raised and lifted up and greatly exalted.
AMP.14:
Just as many were astonished and appalled at you, My people,
So His appearance was marred more than any man
And His form [marred] more than the sons of men.
AMP.15:
So He will sprinkle many nations [with His blood, providing salvation],
Kings will shut their mouths because of Him;
For what they had not been told they will see,
And what they had not heard they will understand.

NIV.1:
Awake, awake, O Zion,
clothe yourself with strength.
Put on your garments of splendor,
O Jerusalem, the holy city.
The uncircumcised and defiled
will not enter you again.
NIV.2:
Shake off your dust;
rise up, sit enthroned, O Jerusalem.
Free yourself from the chains on your neck,
O captive Daughter of Zion.
NIV.3:
For this is what the Lord says:
“You were sold for nothing,
and without money you will be redeemed.”
NIV.4:
For this is what the Sovereign Lord says:
“At first my people went down to Egypt to live;
lately, Assyria has oppressed them.
NIV.5:
“And now what do I have here?” declares the Lord.
“For my people have been taken away for nothing,
and those who rule them mock,”
declares the Lord.
“And all day long
my name is constantly blasphemed.
NIV.6:
Therefore my people will know my name;
therefore in that day they will know
that it is I who foretold it.

How beautiful on the mountains
are the feet of those who bring good news,
who proclaim peace,
who bring good tidings,
who proclaim salvation,
who say to Zion,
“Your God reigns!”
NIV.8:

together they shout for joy.
When the Lord returns to Zion,
they will see it with their own eyes.
NIV.9:
Burst into songs of joy together,
you ruins of Jerusalem,
for the Lord has comforted his people,
he has redeemed Jerusalem.

The Lord will lay bare his holy arm
in the sight of all the nations,
and all the ends of the earth will see
the salvation of our God.

Touch no unclean thing!
Come out from it and be pure,
you who carry the vessels of the Lord.
NIV.12:
But you will not leave in haste
or go in flight;
for the Lord will go before you,

The Suffering and Glory of the Servant

so will he sprinkle many nations,
and kings will shut their mouths because of him.

and what they have not heard, they will understand.

MSG.1:
Wake up, wake up! Pull on your boots, Zion!
Dress up in your Sunday best, Jerusalem, holy city!
Those who want no part of God have been culled out.
They won't be coming along.
MSG.2:
Brush off the dust and get to your feet, captive Jerusalem!
Throw off your chains, captive daughter of Zion!
MSG.3: God says, "You were sold for nothing. You're being bought back for nothing."
MSG.4: Again, the Master, God, says, "Early on, my people went to Egypt and lived, strangers in the land. At the other end, Assyria oppressed them.
MSG.5: And now, what have I here?" God's Decree. "My people are hauled off again for no reason at all. Tyrants on the warpath, whooping it up, and day after day, incessantly, my reputation blackened.
MSG.6: Now it's time that my people know who I am, what I'm made of—yes, that I have something to say. Here I am!"
MSG.7:
How beautiful on the mountains
are the feet of the messenger bringing good news,
Breaking the news that all's well,
proclaiming good times, announcing salvation,
telling Zion, "Your God reigns!"
MSG.8:
Voices! Listen! Your scouts are shouting, thunderclap shouts,
shouting in joyful unison.
They see with their own eyes
God coming back to Zion.
MSG.9:
Break into song! Boom it out, ruins of Jerusalem:
"God has comforted his people!
He's redeemed Jerusalem!"
MSG.10:
God has rolled up his sleeves.
All the nations can see his holy, muscled arm.
Everyone, from one end of the earth to the other,
sees him at work, doing his salvation work.
MSG.11:
Out of here! Out of here! Leave this place!
Don't look back. Don't contaminate yourselves with plunder.
Just leave, but leave clean. Purify yourselves
in the process of worship, carrying the holy vessels of God.
MSG.12:
But you don't have to be in a hurry.
You're not running from anybody!
God is leading you out of here,
and the God of Israel is also your rear guard.
MSG.13:
"Just watch my servant blossom!
Exalted, tall, head and shoulders above the crowd!
MSG.14:
But he didn't begin that way.
At first everyone was appalled.
He didn't even look human—
a ruined face, disfigured past recognition.
MSG.15:
Nations all over the world will be in awe, taken aback,
kings shocked into silence when they see him.
For what was unheard of they'll see with their own eyes,
what was unthinkable they'll have right before them."

NET.2: Shake off the dirt! Get up, captive Jerusalem! Take off the iron chains around your neck, O captive daughter Zion!
NET.3: For this is what the LORD says: “You were sold for nothing, and you will not be redeemed for money.”
NET.4: For this is what the sovereign LORD says: “In the beginning my people went to live temporarily in Egypt; Assyria oppressed them for no good reason.
NET.5: And now, what do we have here?” says the LORD. “Indeed my people have been carried away for nothing, those who rule over them taunt,” says the LORD, “and my name is constantly slandered all day long.
NET.6: For this reason my people will know my name, for this reason they will know at that time that I am the one who says, ‘Here I am.’”
NET.7: How delightful it is to see approaching over the mountains the feet of a messenger who announces peace, a messenger who brings good news, who announces deliverance, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
NET.8: Listen, your watchmen shout; in unison they shout for joy, for they see with their very own eyes the LORD’s return to Zion.
NET.9: In unison give a joyful shout, O ruins of Jerusalem! For the LORD consoles his people; he protects Jerusalem.
NET.10: The LORD reveals his royal power in the sight of all the nations; the entire earth sees our God deliver.
NET.11: Leave! Leave! Get out of there! Don’t touch anything unclean! Get out of it! Stay pure, you who carry the LORD’s holy items!
NET.12: Yet do not depart quickly or leave in a panic. For the LORD goes before you; the God of Israel is your rear guard.
NET.13: “Look, my servant will succeed! He will be elevated, lifted high, and greatly exalted —
NET.14: (just as many were horrified by the sight of you) he was so disfigured he no longer looked like a man;
NET.15: his form was so marred he no longer looked human — so now he will startle many nations. Kings will be shocked by his exaltation, for they will witness something unannounced to them, and they will understand something they had not heard about.

NRSVCE.1:
Awake, awake,
put on your strength, O Zion!
Put on your beautiful garments,
O Jerusalem, the holy city;
for the uncircumcised and the unclean
shall enter you no more.
NRSVCE.2:
Shake yourself from the dust, rise up,
O captive Jerusalem;
loose the bonds from your neck,
O captive daughter Zion!
NRSVCE.3: For thus says the LORD: You were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without money.
NRSVCE.4: For thus says the Lord GOD: Long ago, my people went down into Egypt to reside there as aliens; the Assyrian, too, has oppressed them without cause.
NRSVCE.5: Now therefore what am I doing here, says the LORD, seeing that my people are taken away without cause? Their rulers howl, says the LORD, and continually, all day long, my name is despised.
NRSVCE.6: Therefore my people shall know my name; therefore in that day they shall know that it is I who speak; here am I.
NRSVCE.7:
How beautiful upon the mountains
are the feet of the messenger who announces peace,
who brings good news,
who announces salvation,
who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
NRSVCE.8:
Listen! Your sentinels lift up their voices,
together they sing for joy;
for in plain sight they see
the return of the LORD to Zion.
NRSVCE.9:
Break forth together into singing,
you ruins of Jerusalem;
for the LORD has comforted his people,
he has redeemed Jerusalem.
NRSVCE.10:
The LORD has bared his holy arm
before the eyes of all the nations;
and all the ends of the earth shall see
the salvation of our God.
NRSVCE.11:
Depart, depart, go out from there!
Touch no unclean thing;
go out from the midst of it, purify yourselves,
you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
NRSVCE.12:
For you shall not go out in haste,
and you shall not go in flight;
for the LORD will go before you,
and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
NRSVCE.13:
See, my servant shall prosper;
he shall be exalted and lifted up,
and shall be very high.
NRSVCE.14:
Just as there were many who were astonished at him
— so marred was his appearance, beyond human semblance,
and his form beyond that of mortals —
NRSVCE.15:
so he shall startle many nations;
kings shall shut their mouths because of him;
for that which had not been told them they shall see,
and that which they had not heard they shall contemplate.
